newsitem.title: UK: British mortgage lenders launch code of practice.
newsitem.headline: British mortgage lenders launch code of practice.

text.p: Britain's Council of Mortgage Lenders on Saturday launched a new code of practice providing a complete benchmark of minimum standards which mortgage lenders will follow.

The code covers the whole mortgage lending process, from marketing, through the sales process, to the lender's handling of the customer's affairs and any complaints or financial difficulties that may apply.
It was welcomed by consumers and practitioners alike, but the Consumers' Association said the code is not completely watertight.

It said some mortgage advisers such as mortgage brokers and independent financial advisers could slip through the net as CML's rules do not apply to them and they may be able to escape the Code's vital "best advice" requirement.

The CML said it has recognised the fact that as many as 50 percent of mortgages that are sold by intermediaries and said it has set up a working group to draw up detailed proposals on a registration scheme for intermediaries.

But the Consumers' Association said the resulting code is unlikely to have enough power and that regulations under the Financial Services Act would be the best way to cover the actions of all mortgage advisers.
The Code will come into effect on July 1, 1997 and has been produced at the same time as a revision of the Banking Code which covers banking practice more generally.
